# PRJNA896566 — cereal field RNA-seq cohort evidence

*Generated by `report/build_release.py` from the curation seeds. Do not edit.*

- **Organism:** Zea mays
- **Runs in cohort:** 72  (Maize 72)
- **Discovery route:** accession_list
- **Papers:** 10.1093/plphys/kiad460 (10.1093/plphys/kiad460)

## setting
**72 run(s)** — rule `kiad23-setting` — 10.1093/plphys/kiad460  
*Materials and methods, 'Data and tissue collection for physiological, metabolic, and transcriptome analyses'*

> Maize (Z. mays) inbred lines B73 and Mo17 were grown in a randomized complete block factorial design with 3 replications and 2 treatments at SIMPSON RESEARCH FARM, PENDLETON, SC, USA, IN THE SUMMER OF 2017. In each block, each inbred line was grown in two 6-row plots with row and row-to-row distances of 4.57 and 0.762 m, respectively, and the 2 treatments, pollinated and nonpollinated, were randomly assigned to the plots. The primary and secondary ears of all plants in all plots were covered with shoot bags before silk emergence, and the treatments were started at 0 DAA characterized by silks emergence in >=80% of the plants... Data collection and sampling were performed on the leaf at 2 nodes above the ear-bearing node of 2 competitive randomly chosen plants at 3-d intervals from 0 to 45 DAA... The leaf samples consisting of 30 cm of the leaf blade excluding midrib, ligule, and sheath were chopped into small pieces, flash frozen.
